verses.zh: 约瑟伏在他父亲的面上哀哭，与他亲嘴。
verses.en: Then Joseph hugged his father’s face.[NOTE:1] He wept over him and kissed him.
notes: Heb “fell on.” The expression describes Joseph’s unrestrained sorrow over Jacob’s death; he probably threw himself across the body and embraced his father.
verses.commentary:
50:1 This verse shows three signs of grieving associated with death.

- fell on his father's face, BDB 656, KB 709, Qal IMPERFECT with waw,
similar to 33:4

- wept over him, BDB 113, KB 129, Qal IMPERFECT with waw

- kissed him, BDB 676, KB 730, Qal IMPERFECT with waw

verses.zh: 约瑟吩咐伺候他的医生用香料薰他父亲，医生就用香料薰了以色列。
verses.en: Joseph instructed the physicians in his service[NOTE:1] to embalm his father, so the physicians embalmed Israel.
notes: Heb “his servants the physicians.”
verses.commentary:
50:2 "physicians" This is a Qal ACTIVE PARTICIPLE of the VERB "to
heal" (BDB 950, KB 1272, cf. 2 Chr. 16:12). There was a group of professional embalmers, but Joseph possibly
used physicians in order to side step the religious overtones of Egyptian embalming (NASB Study Bible,
p. 73). Jacob was preserved so that he could later be buried in the family burial cave in Canaan
(cf. Gen. 49:29-32).

▣ "embalm" This VERB (BDB 334, KB 333, Qal INFINITIVE
CONSTRUCTY) means "spice," "make spice" (cf. Song of Songs 2:13), or "embalm." This was a
uniquely Egyptian procedure, found only here in the OT. It had religious connections to Osiris
(beginning about 2700 B.C.) and the Egyptians' belief in an afterlife.

It involved

- the removal of the internal organs and their separate preservation in jars

- in a later period the brain was also removed and placed in a separate jar

- the body was wrapped with resinated linen cloth

The only written accounts of how to embalm come from Herodotus, History 2:85-90 and
Diodorus Siculus, History 1.91. For a fuller discussion see ABD, vol. 2, pp. 490-495, and James M.
Freeman, Manners and Customs of the Bible, pp. 56-58.

This discussion is not meant in any way to address modern embalming practices. They have
no religious overtones as did the Egyptian rituals. Many have assumed that the curse statement in Gen. 3:19
still applies. I personally think the physical remains of life (i.e., human bodies) are not that significant!

verses.zh: 薰尸的常例是四十天；那四十天满了，埃及人为他哀哭了七十天。
verses.en: They took 40 days, for that is the full time needed for embalming.[NOTE:1] The Egyptians mourned for[NOTE:2] him 70 days.[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “and forty days were fulfilled for him, for thus are fulfilled the days of embalming.”
Heb “wept for.”
Seventy days. This probably refers to a time of national mourning.
verses.commentary:
50:3 "forty days" The number 40 (BDB 917) can be literal or figurative. The Hebrews mourned for 30
days (cf. Num. 20:29; Deut. 34:8) for national leaders. It was a sign of respect.

▣ "seventy days" Jacob received a royal burial. Pharaoh himself was mourned for seventy-two days
(the Greek historian, Diodorus [1.72]). The Egyptians mourned for Jacob out of respect for Joseph.

verses.zh: 为他哀哭的日子过了，约瑟对法老家中的人说：「我若在你们眼前蒙恩，请你们报告法老说：『
verses.en: When the days of mourning[NOTE:1] had passed, Joseph said to Pharaoh’s royal court,[NOTE:2] “If I have found favor in your sight, please say to Pharaoh,[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “weeping.”
Heb “the house of Pharaoh.”
Heb “in the ears of Pharaoh.”
verses.commentary:
50:4 "favor in your sight" This is an idiom of approval (cf. Gen. 18:3; 47:29; Exod. 33:13). This
idiom is always used of an inferior asking a superior (i.e., Ruth 2:13). Here Joseph is showing respect
for Pharaoh.

verses.zh: 我父亲要死的时候叫我起誓说：你要将我葬在迦南地，在我为自己所掘的坟墓里。』现在求你让我上去葬我父亲，以后我必回来。」
verses.en: ‘My father made me swear an oath. He said,[NOTE:1] “I am about to die. Bury me[NOTE:2] in my tomb that I dug for myself there in the land of Canaan.” Now let me go and bury my father; then I will return.’”
notes: Heb “saying.”
The imperfect verbal form here has the force of a command.
verses.commentary:
50:5-6 In Gen. 50:5 Joseph shares his oath (BDB 989, KB 1396, two Hiphil PERFECTS,
Gen. 50:5,6) to his father, Jacob (#1,2) and a promise to return (#3).

- go up, BDB 748, KB 828, Qal IMPERFECT used in a COHORTATIVE
sense

- bury me, BDB 868, KB 1064, Qal COHORTATIVE

- I will return, BDB 996, KB 1427, Qal COHORTATIVE

In Gen. 50:6 Pharaoh responds to his request related to his oath.

- go up, Qal IMPERATIVE

- bury, Qal IMPERATIVE

50:5

NASB, NKJV, NJB, LXX
"dug"

NRSV
"hewed out"

TEV
"he had prepared"

REB, Peshitta
"bought"

JPSOA
"made ready"

The Rabbinical Midrash (Peshitta and REV) replaces this term with "bought"
(cf. Gen. 23:17-20; 47:27-31; 49:29-32). The two Hebrew roots are the same

- dig, BDB 500 I, cf. Gen. 26:25; Num. 21:18

- buy, BDB 500 II, cf. Deut. 2:6

verses.zh: 法老说：「你可以上去，照着你父亲叫你起的誓，将他葬埋。」
verses.en: So Pharaoh said, “Go and bury your father, just as he made you swear to do.”[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “he made you swear on oath.”

verses.zh: 于是约瑟上去葬他父亲。与他一同上去的，有法老的臣仆和法老家中的长老，并埃及国的长老，
verses.en: So Joseph went up to bury his father; all Pharaoh’s officials went with him—the senior courtiers[NOTE:1] of his household, all the senior officials of the land of Egypt,
notes: Or “dignitaries”; Heb “elders.”
verses.commentary:
50:7-8 Verses 7-8 show how large a funeral possession went to Canaan.

- Joseph

- the servants of Pharaoh

- the elders of his household

- the elders of the land of Egypt

- household of Joseph

- Joseph's brothers

- Jacob's household

- a military escort, Gen. 50:9

Verse 9 implies a military escort. It may also have been Pharaoh's way to assure the return of
his best administrator/advisor.

verses.zh: 还有约瑟的全家和他的弟兄们，并他父亲的眷属；只有他们的妇人孩子，和羊群牛群，都留在歌珊地。
verses.en: all Joseph’s household, his brothers, and his father’s household. But they left their little children and their flocks and herds in the land of Goshen.
verses.commentary:
50:8 "They left only their little ones and their flocks" This was to assure their return!

▣ "in the land of Goshen" See notes at Gen. 45:10; 46:28.

verses.zh: 又有车辆马兵，和他一同上去；那一帮人甚多。
verses.en: Chariots and horsemen also went up with him, so it was a very large entourage.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “camp.”
verses.commentary:
50:9 "chariots and horsemen" See
SPECIAL TOPIC: CHARIOTS

verses.zh: 他们到了约旦河外、亚达的禾场，就在那里大大地号啕痛哭。约瑟为他父亲哀哭了七天。
verses.en: When they came to the threshing floor of Atad[NOTE:1] on the other side of the Jordan, they mourned there with very great and bitter sorrow.[NOTE:2] There Joseph observed a seven-day period of mourning for his father.
notes: The location of the threshing floor of Atad is not certain. The expression the other side of the Jordan could refer to the eastern or western bank, depending on one’s perspective. However, it is commonly used in the OT for Transjordan. This would suggest that the entourage came up the Jordan Valley and crossed into the land at Jericho, just as the Israelites would in the time of Joshua.
Heb “and they mourned there [with] very great and heavy mourning.” The cognate accusative, as well as the two adjectives and the adverb, emphasize the degree of their sorrow.
verses.commentary:
50:10 "Atad" Literally this is "thorns" (BDB 31). The Rabbinical Midrash says it was a protective
hedge. This site is unknown. Jerome says it was located near Jericho. It was the site of a ritual mourning,
not necessarily the site of the burial!

▣ The intensity of their grief is described by

- they lamented there

- with a very great

- and mournful

- lamentation

- observed seven days

- note Gen. 50:11

▣ "beyond the Jordan" This phrase, "in the region of" (BDB 81 CONSTRUCT BDB 719 I,
cf. Gen. 50:11), does not determine the east or west bank. It depends on the location of the speaker.

verses.zh: 迦南的居民见亚达禾场上的哀哭，就说：「这是埃及人一场极大的哀哭。」因此那地方名叫亚伯・麦西，是在约旦河东。
verses.en: When the Canaanites who lived in the land saw them mourning at the threshing floor of Atad, they said, “This is a very sad occasion[NOTE:1] for the Egyptians.” That is why its name was called[NOTE:2] Abel Mizraim,[NOTE:3] which is beyond the Jordan.
notes: Heb “this is heavy mourning for Egypt.”
The verb has no expressed subject and so it may be translated as passive.
The name Abel Mizraim means “the mourning of Egypt.”
verses.commentary:
50:11 This is a play on the word "Abel" (BDB 5 II), which means "meadow" (lit. "grow green grass"),
and "Abel" (BDB 5 I), which means "mourning" (AB lists a third option, "watercourse," p. 376).

verses.zh: 雅各的儿子们就遵着他父亲所吩咐的办了，
verses.en: So the sons of Jacob did for him just as he had instructed them.
verses.commentary: 50:12-14 This is a summary statement describing their promise to Jacob.

verses.zh: 把他搬到迦南地，葬在幔利前、麦比拉田间的洞里；那洞和田是亚伯拉罕向赫人以弗仑买来为业，作坟地的。
verses.en: His sons carried him to the land of Canaan and buried him in the cave of the field of Machpelah, near Mamre. This is the field Abraham purchased as a burial plot from Ephron the Hittite.
verses.commentary: 50:13 "the cave" This cave is the one referred to in Gen. 23:16-20.

verses.zh: 约瑟葬了他父亲以后，就和众弟兄，并一切同他上去葬他父亲的人，都回埃及去了。
verses.en: After he buried his father, Joseph returned to Egypt, along with his brothers and all who had accompanied him to bury his father.

verses.zh: 约瑟的哥哥们见父亲死了，就说：「或者约瑟怀恨我们，照着我们从前待他一切的恶足足地报复我们。」
verses.en: When Joseph’s brothers saw that their father was dead, they said, “What if Joseph bears a grudge and wants to repay[NOTE:1] us in full[NOTE:2] for all the harm[NOTE:3] we did to him?”
notes: The imperfect tense could be a simple future; it could also have a desiderative nuance.
The infinitive absolute makes the statement emphatic, “repay in full.”
Or “evil.”
verses.commentary:
50:15 The intensity of the brothers' concern is expressed in

- the VERB "bear a grudge" (BDB 966, KB 1316), which was used earlier of Esau (Gen. 27:41)
and alluded to in Gen. 49:23. It is also used by Job 16:9; 30:21. It is a very strong
VERB.

- the phrase "and pay us back in full," which is a Hiphil INFINITIVE ABSOLUTE and
a Hiphil IMPERFECT of the same root (BDB 996, KB 1427).

verses.zh: 他们就打发人去见约瑟，说：「你父亲未死以先吩咐说：『
verses.en: So they sent word[NOTE:1] to Joseph, saying, “Your father gave these instructions before he died:
notes: The verb means “command,” but they would hardly be commanding him. It probably means they sent their father’s instructions to Joseph.
verses.commentary:
50:16-17 This introduces an unknown quote from Jacob which the brothers were quoting to assure
Joseph's favor.

verses.zh: 你们要对约瑟这样说：从前你哥哥们恶待你，求你饶恕他们的过犯和罪恶。』如今求你饶恕你父亲　神之仆人的过犯。」他们对约瑟说这话，约瑟就哭了。
verses.en: ‘Tell Joseph this: Please forgive the sin of your brothers and the wrong they did when they treated you so badly.’ Now please forgive the sin of the servants of the God of your father.” When this message was reported to him, Joseph wept.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “and Joseph wept when they spoke to him.”
verses.commentary:
50:17 This verse sets the stage for Joseph's faith statement in Gen. 50:19-20. The brothers' fear
and desire for forgiveness can be seen in

- please forgive, BDB 609, KB 724, Qal IMPERATIVE

- I beg you (NASB expansion)

- the transgression and sin of your brothers (cf. Gen. 37:18-28)

- (we) did wrong

- please forgive the transgression

- v. 18

The only reasons for their request were

- Jacob's words, Gen. 50:16-17

- they are servants of the God of Jacob, Gen. 50:17

verses.zh: 他的哥哥们又来俯伏在他面前，说：「我们是你的仆人。」
verses.en: Then his brothers also came and threw themselves down before him; they said, “Here we are; we are your slaves.”

verses.zh: 约瑟对他们说：「不要害怕，我岂能代替　神呢？
verses.en: But Joseph answered them, “Don’t be afraid. Am[NOTE:1] I in the place of God?
notes: Heb “For am I.”
verses.commentary:
50:19

NASB, NKJV, NRSV
"for am I in God's place"

TEV
"I can't put myself in the place of God"

NJB
"is it for me to put myself in God's place"

LXX
"for I am God's"

Peshitta
"for I am a servant of God"

JPSOA
"Am I a substitute for God"

This was Joseph's way of saying that he saw himself as part of God's method for
preserving Abraham's family (cf. Gen. 45:5-15; Ps. 105:16-24)! He explains this in Gen. 50:20. He did
not see himself as acting as judge, only God can do this! The question in Hebrew expects a "no" answer.
This same expression is found in Gen. 30:2.

verses.zh: 从前你们的意思是要害我，但　神的意思原是好的，要保全许多人的性命，成就今日的光景。
verses.en: As for you, you meant to harm me,[NOTE:1] but God intended it for a good purpose, so he could preserve the lives of many people, as you can see this day.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “you devised against me evil.”
Heb “God devised it for good in order to do, like this day, to preserve alive a great nation.”
verses.commentary:
50:20 "you meant evil against me" Joseph did not cover over the brothers' sin, but saw the "unseen
hand" of God in his life and circumstances! Oh that we could, by faith, recognize the "unseen hand" in our
lives!

For a good article on God using the sin of humans to accomplish His purposes, see Millard
Erickson, Christian Theology, second ed., pp. 425-426.

▣ "God meant it for good" This is a good example of the meaning of Romans 8:28-29.

verses.zh: 现在你们不要害怕，我必养活你们和你们的妇人孩子。」于是约瑟用亲爱的话安慰他们。
verses.en: So now, don’t be afraid. I will provide for you and your little children.” Then he consoled them and spoke kindly to them.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “spoke to their heart.”
verses.commentary:
50:21 Joseph tells them what he will do for the family.

- do not be afraid, BDB 431, KB 432, Qal IMPERFECT used in a
JUSSIVE sense, as in Gen. 50:19; see
SPECIAL TOPIC: FEAR (OT)

- I will provide for you, BDB 465, KB 463, Pilpel IMPERFECT, cf. Gen. 45:11;
47:12

- I will provide for your little ones, BDB 465, KB 463, Pilpel IMPERFECT,
cf. Gen. 45:11; 47:12

- he comforted them, BDB 636, KB 688, Piel IMPERFECT with waw; see
SPECIAL TOPIC: COMFORT

- spoke kindly to them (lit. "speak to the heart" (BDB 180, KB 210, Piel IMPERFECT
with waw, cf. Gen. 34:3; Jdg. 19:3; Ruth 2:13)

verses.zh: 约瑟和他父亲的眷属都住在埃及。约瑟活了一百一十岁。
verses.en: Joseph lived in Egypt, along with his father’s family.[NOTE:1] Joseph lived 110 years.
notes: Heb “he and the house of his father.”
verses.commentary: 50:22 "one hundred and ten years" This was the ideal age in Egyptian literature of the period.

verses.zh: 约瑟得见以法莲第三代的子孙。玛拿西的孙子、玛吉的儿子也养在约瑟的膝上。
verses.en: Joseph saw the descendants of Ephraim to the third generation.[NOTE:1] He also saw the children of Makir the son of Manasseh; they were given special inheritance rights by Joseph.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “saw Ephraim, the children of the third.”

Heb “generation. Also the sons of Machir, the son of Manasseh, were born on the knees of Joseph.” The expression "born on the knees" implies their adoption by Joseph, which meant that they received an inheritance from him.
verses.commentary:
50:23 "Machir" Also see Joshua 17:1 and Judges 5:14. The name may be related to the similar root for
"merchandise" or "value" (BDB 569).

▣ "born on Joseph's knee" Obviously this was not to be taken literally. It is a cultural ANE
idiom used for adoption (cf. Gen. 30:3; 48:12) or receiving someone into the family.

verses.zh: 约瑟对他弟兄们说：「我要死了，但　神必定看顾你们，领你们从这地上去，到他起誓所应许给亚伯拉罕、以撒、雅各之地。」
verses.en: Then Joseph said to his brothers, “I am about to die. But God will surely come to you[NOTE:1] and lead you up from this land to the land he swore on oath to give[NOTE:2] to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.”
notes: The verb פָּקַד (paqad) means “to visit,” i.e., to intervene for blessing or cursing; here Joseph announces that God would come to fulfill the promises by delivering them from Egypt. The statement is emphasized by the use of the infinitive absolute with the verb: “God will surely visit you.”
The words “to give” are supplied in the translation for clarity and for stylistic reasons.
verses.commentary:
50:24 "God will surely take care of you" Joseph trusted in God's promised care for Abraham's family
(cf. Gen. 15:16)! Joseph was God's instrument, but as he passed from this life, God would raise up others
(i.e., Moses, Aaron, Joshua, etc.).

Joseph's words are intensified by the Qal INFINITIVE ABSOLUTE and
Qal IMPERFECT VERB of the same root (BDB 823, KB 955, lit, "visit," used in a
specialized sense of God's personal presence and care, cf. Exod. 3:16; 4:31; Ruth 1:6; Zeph. 2:7). This
form is found in both Gen. 50:24,25!

TOPIC: COVENANT PROMISES TO THE PATRIARCHS

verses.zh: 约瑟叫以色列的子孙起誓说：「　神必定看顾你们；你们要把我的骸骨从这里搬上去。」
verses.en: Joseph made the sons of Israel swear an oath. He said, “God will surely come to you. Then you must carry my bones up from this place.”
verses.commentary:
50:25 "carry my bones" He knew they would return to the promised land and he wanted to be buried
there just as his father had been (cf. Exod. 13:19; Jos. 24:32).

verses.zh: 约瑟死了，正一百一十岁。人用香料将他薰了，把他收殓在棺材里，停在埃及。
verses.en: So Joseph died at the age of 110. After[NOTE:1] they embalmed him, his body[NOTE:2] was placed in a coffin in Egypt.
notes: Heb “son of a hundred and ten years.”
Heb “he.”
verses.commentary:
50:26 "coffin" This word (BDB 75) can refer to

- ark (of the covenant, i.e., Exod. 25:22; 26:33; 30:6; Num. 10:33; Deut. 10:8; 31:9; Josh 3:3), a
religious sacred box

- coffin, only here (Israelites did not use coffins)

- chest, for money (i.e., 2 Kgs. 12:10; 2 Chr. 24:8,10,11)

The other word translated in English "ark" (BDB 1061) refers to

- Noah's ark (i.e., Gen. 6:14)

- Moses' papyrus crib (i.e., Exod. 2:3)

WORD AND PHRASE STUDY

NASB (UPDATED) TEXT: GENESIS 50:1-3

1Then Joseph fell on his father's face, and wept over him and kissed him. 2Joseph commanded his servants the physicians to embalm his father. So the physicians embalmed Israel. 3Now forty days were required for it, for such is the period required for embalming. And the Egyptians wept for him seventy days.
